Tuairisc Bhainistíochta Mhíosúil an Príomhfheidhmeannach – 30ú Samhain 2025 
Chief Executive’s Monthly Management Report – 30th November 2025 
 
 
 
A Chara, 
 
I enclose the above report for your statutory consideration, this report has also been prepared under Section 136 
& 138 of the Local Government Act, 2001. The attached report is the Chief Executive’s Monthly Management 
Report for November 2025, detailing activities, updates and progress across various departments of Louth 
County Council.  
 
Key achievements and actions under various directorates from the Chief Executive Report for November 2025: 
 
1. Finance and System Support Directorate 
• 
Louth County Council’s Budget was passed by the members on 17th November 2025. 
• 
Expenditure to date: €160M (87% of budget spent); Income to date: €154M (84% invoiced). 
• 
Debtors balance: €52.6M; 83% of IT support calls resolved. 
• 
Between 1st to 30th November, there were 646 support calls logged in the IT support system, 83% of 
these calls have been completed. 
• 
Roll out of cyber training continues for both the councillors and the executive. 
 
2. Economic Delivery Directorate 
• 
Rates Waiver Scheme 2026 proposed by the Economic Development & Enterprise Support SPC was 
approved at the 2026 Budget. 
• 
Hosted Northeast Business Awards and supported tourism initiatives like Frostival Winter Festival 
and Boyne Valley Flavours. 
• 
The Council provided financial and operational support for ‘The Mass of the Bells’ that was broadcast 
live on RTÉ from St. Peter’s Catholic Church, Drogheda on Sunday 23rd November. 
• 
LEO Louth sponsored Dundalk Chamber’s Auto-Enrolment Breakfast, where 170 local businesses 
came together to prepare for upcoming workplace pension changes. 
• 
Drogheda Digital Innovation Hub kicked off the first of the DigiBytes workshops on Thursday, 6th 
November. 
• 
In October 2025, 89 planning applications were received, 76 were valid, there were 35 responses for 
further information and 21 pre-planning requests received. 
 
3. Operations & Environment Delivery Directorate 
• 
Extensive road repairs, drainage remediation and illegal dumping cleanups across municipal districts 
were ongoing throughout the month. 
• 
Enhanced public spaces, including Muirhevnamor Park and Carlingford Laneways. 
• 
Waste enforcement handled 264 complaints, 23 diesel laundering drums removed. 
• 
Climate action initiatives included stakeholder engagement and solar PV installations. 
• 
Building Works to renovate and improve the Council’s existing Cornmarket Building at Fair Street 
Drogheda are in progress and the works are expected to be completed before end 2025. 
• 
Works to repair the wall leading to the Tower at Millmount are almost complete.

4. HR, Corporate & Community Delivery Directorate 
• 
Customer Services handled 19,660 queries; 59% (11,654) resolved at first contact. 
• 
Supported community projects like Age Friendly workshops, Louth Comhairle na nÓg and Healthy Louth 
initiatives. 
• 
On 19th November, the annual Community & Voluntary Awards took place in Monasterboice, celebrating 
the dedication of voluntary groups across the County. 
• 
Launched the Tidy Towns Project Scheme 2026. 
• 
LAG approved €218,752.84 in funding for 7 LEADER projects under the themes of: Rural Infrastructure 
& Social Inclusion and Rural Environment and Climate Change. This brings total LEADER funding 
allocated in Louth to €1,201,645.50. 
 
5. Housing & Culture Delivery Directorate 
• Addressed homelessness with 194 presentations and 33 emergency placements. 
• Delivered 283 social housing units in 2025, exceeding targets. 
• Managed €4m in rent arrears and processed 985 maintenance requests. 
• Supported cultural initiatives like Louth Science Festival and library outreach programs. 
 
 
6. Major Capital Projects & Infrastructure Delivery Directorate 
• Progressed major projects including the Narrow Water Bridge, Dundalk-Carlingford Greenway and flood 
relief schemes. 
• Advanced Active Travel projects, including safe routes to schools and mobility hubs. 
• Delivered urban regeneration plans for Dundalk, Drogheda and Ardee. 
 
 
This report highlights some of the Louth County Council's progress across the various directorates in November 
2025 
 
I would like extend my heartfelt thanks to all Louth County Council staff for their dedication and hard work 
throughout 2025.  Your efforts have been instrumental in achieving the milestones recorded throughout the year. 
 
May I wish all councillors, staff and the community a very Merry Christmas and a peaceful New Year!

Cyber Security Training – November 
 
This month’s training focused on safeguarding data on mobile devices, including laptops, smartphones, and 
tablets. It highlighted the risks associated with using these devices on unsecured public Wi-Fi networks, 
emphasising that cyber criminals can intercept sensitive information without needing physical access to the 
device.

Purple Flag / Retail Community Safety Session – 
17th November 
The Drogheda Purple Flag group trialed a one-off 
joint meeting with the Garda Retail Community 
Safety group, co-ordinated by Love Drogheda BID, 
to explore joint working and shared challenges.  
Purple Flag recognises towns that offer a safe and 
well-managed evening and night-time environment, 
and this session helped the group better understand 
retail safety issues and reporting challenges.  The 
meeting also considered retail businesses signing 
up to the Purple Flag Charter – a simple commitment 
to safety, inclusivity and partnership – and 
developing a brief toolkit to support reporting and 
access to Garda assistance, such as via Crime 
Reduction Officers.  The session was seen as a 
positive step in strengthening collaboration across 
retail, hospitality and safety partners.

‘Intervals of Peace’ Exhibition 
The launch of a new exhibition: “Intervals of Peace: 
The Civil War Prison Art of Alfred McGloughlin” took 
place on November 11 at Louth County Archives. 
The exhibition was officially opened by Cllr Dolores 
Minogue, Cathaoirleach of Ardee Municipal District, 
David Conway, Chief Executive of Louth County 
Council, and Professor Tim McGloughlin, grandson 
of the artist.  
 
Alfred McGloughlin, who was an artist and a nephew 
of the leader of the 1916 Rising, Patrick Pearse, was 
an anti-Treaty supporter during the Civil War. While 
he was imprisoned from 1922 to 1923, he kept up his 
artistic endeavours by drawing fellow prisoners. 
Speaking at the opening of the exhibition Prof Tim 
McGloughlin said:  
“It’s incredibly meaningful to see my grandfather’s 
artwork now on display in Dundalk, in a space with 
its own deep ties to Ireland’s revolutionary history. 
These drawings, created during some of the 
darkest days of the Civil War, reflect not only
